```text
#### **5. INSTRUCTIONS TO BIDDERS**

##### 5.1 **Communications** 

All communications and Bidder enquiries in connection with this RFT must be sent in writing to the address set out in the Company Contact Details section of the RFT Summary in Section 4 of this RFT ("**RFT Summary**").

##### 5.2 **English Language** 

All documents and correspondence relating to this RFT shall be in English language. If any documentation relating to this RFT is submitted by the Bidder in another language in addition to English, the English version shall take precedence and be used for interpreting the information.

##### 5.3 **Facsimile / email not acceptable**

Submission of the Bid should be in accordance with the requirements set out in the RFT Summary. Facsimile or email submission of any Bid is not acceptable.
```

```text
Bidder is required to submit its Bid in the following two submissions, in closed envelopes, in accordance with the following two stage bidding process:

To be submitted in accordance with:
```

```text
## **1 GENERAL**

# **1.1 INTRODUCTION**

ADNOC LNG (hereinafter called COMPANY) operates three (3) gas processing Trains in Das Island to produce LNG, LPG, Paraffinic Naphtha, and Sulphur. The Das Island facilities receive the feed gas from ADNOC OFFSHORE. Trains 1 & 2 were built in 1974-1976 with production capacity of 2.9 million tons/year of Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG). The 3rd LNG Train was built in 1991-1994 with an annual capacity of 3.2 million tons.
```

```text
The Trains were commissioned in 1976. In year 2000, a study was undertaken (called Plant Integrity, Reliability and Recertification or PIRR) to extend the operational life of LNG Trains 1 and 2 to year 2019. Thereafter, the Operational life of Trains 1&2 was again extended to 2024 with required replacement / rejuvenation of the systems.

Majority of the process equipment, vessels and columns were replaced during the LNG Trains 1&2 Turnarounds which will have remnant life well beyond 2024.

As part of strategic requirement, ADNOC LNG launched in 2018 its Asset Longevity Program to extend the operation life of its three (3) LNG Trains year 2040. The Asset Longevity Program comprises of the following Work Streams:
```

```text
Work stream 3 is the main scope of Rejuvenation Project. In addition, Total Sulphur Reduction (TSR) Project from Work Stream 4 will be included as part of Rejuvenation Project, while Work stream -2 (TA scope) and various other schemes will also be implemented during common Shutdown.

At present, total Sulphur content in the produced LNG lies in the range 4-9 mg/Nm3. Due to prevailing LNG market scenarios, COMPANY shall export LNG with an improved quality requirement (total Sulphur content in LNG shall be less than 1 mg/Nm3).

Following the detailed feasibility study outcomes, COMPANY decided to pursue UOP (Process Licensor) Option and undertake a fast-track Front End Engineering Design followed through Detail Engineering & Procurement Services of major items. The schedule shall enable the PROJECT to be implemented during the planned shutdowns for Trains 1 & 2 in 2025.
```

```text
# **1.2 PROJECT OBJECTIVE**

The objective of the Project is to Repair / Rejuvenate LNG Trains 1 & 2 identified equipment, and extend the operation life till year 2040 whilst optimizing the common shutdown related work duration in order to avoid consequent production losses to the COMPANY, while maintaining the Plant reliability and availability and improving the quality of LNG through implementing TSR modifications for Trains 1&2.

This document, contains only a brief EPC Scope of Work (SOW), is issued for high level understanding of the Project scope and to provide a summary of the Engineering, Procurement and Construction activities for Train 1 and 2 to be executed by EPC CONTRACTOR

EPC CONTRACTOR shall provide and execute the Project WORKS based on the requirements stipulated in this document as well as other documents provided as part of EPC Tender package.
```

```text
# **SCOPE OF ENGINEERING SERVICES FOR HOME OFFICE AND FIELD CONTRACTOR shall perform the following, as applicable.**

# **3A-4.1 GENERAL**

It is a mandatory COMPANY requirement that CONTRACTOR perform the following:

- i. The detailed engineering is to be managed and coordinated by CONTRACTOR.
- ii. The detailed engineering is to be carried out from a single location, and organized on a task force basis at CONTRACTOR's Home Office, unless otherwise agreed in writing.
```

```text
# **3A-4.2 DETAILED ENGINEERING**

# **3A-4.2.1 Design Philosophy and Criteria**

The PLANT shall be designed and engineered in conformity with this document and the requirements set forth in the specifications and standards, design codes, recommended practices, safety design codes, included elsewhere in this AGREEMENT.

The requirements of Codes and Standards stated in the AGREEMENT are the minimum requirements with deviations or enhancements, subject to COMPANY's approval. Due care shall be exercised such that the PLANT affords ease of modularization, construction and expansion, COMMISSIONING and start-up, repair and maintenance, (including provision of permanent craneage and hoisting equipment) and shall be safe to operate under all conditions and for personnel to work in. Consideration shall also be given to the following in the design of SYSTEMS:

- The PROJECT is to be engineered in accordance with the PROJECT specifications and standards. Any deviations require prior COMPANY approval.
- Local environmental conditions and regulations must be strictly adhered to.
- No environmental hazards are to be created to upset the ecology of the surroundings.
- The PLANT, including all buildings and structures, as designed, shall be capable of safe and efficient operations for the entire life of PLANT, which is a minimum of 30 years.
```

```text
CONTRACTOR shall perform Electrical Engineering including but not limited to the following:
```

```text
# **3A-3.2.3.12 Instrumentation, Control Systems Engineering and Telecoms**

Instrumentation and Control Systems scope of work shall include all the engineering, design, procurement, and installation requirements of field instrumentation, control and monitoring systems, emergency shutdown systems, fire and gas detection systems, and fire alarm systems. It shall also include the engineering, design, procurement and installation requirements of the telecommunication systems, including CCTV, radio, telephone, etc.

The CONTRACTOR is to note that the following services apply to all plant equipment inclusive of VENDOR furnished packaged equipment. The specifications, data sheets, drawings, etc. for the PROJECT shall be prepared as integrated documents covering both the main plant and packaged unit equipment. It is the CONTRACTOR's responsibility to issue standard formats / blanks to ensure strict compliance with this requirement from the issue of specifications and enquiries to all SUBCONTRACTORS and VENDORS, to production of PROJECT as built documents.

![](_page_248_Picture_0.jpeg)

The CONTRACTOR shall ensure that the Distributed Control System VENDOR integrates all subsidiary control systems (e.g. Emergency Shutdown (ESD) and Fire and Gas (F&G) systems) into the main Distributed Control System (DCS).

CONTRACTOR shall carry out all modifications required to existing systems in order to meet the PROJECT requirement.
```

```text
- Update Relief and Blow down Philosophies
- Design and verify over-pressure protection systems.
- Ensure adherence to good practice and safety design codes.

- Update drawings to "as-built" stage.
- Prepare control logic diagrams.
- Review instrument and equipment location drawings to ensure quick and easy operations access to valve stations and instruments.
- Installation and construction specifications and drawings
```

```text
## **3A-4.2.3.16.4 Quantitative Risk Assessment**

CONTRACTOR shall undertake an integrated QRA to assess the impact of the complete range of potential hazards associated with the facility to people

![](_page_20_Picture_0.jpeg)

during Construction and Operation phases. It shall investigate the overall result of the Formal Safety Assessment (FSA) program. Risk to people shall be calculated in the form of Individual risk for personnel and the plant and shall demonstrate that individual and societal risks to personnel are within COMPANY risk acceptability.

CONTRACTOR shall use the FEED Quantitative Risk Assessments as basis to develop a complete assessment with the information available during the detail design. The QRA shall consider the risk to personnel from all major risk contributors.

CONTRACTOR shall review the future modifications to the facility for their impact on the QRA and wherever possible, ALARP solutions adopted.

The QRA shall as a minimum include:

- Fire Risk Analysis (FRA) (to assess the consequences of fires initiated from failure of process plant, pipelines, hydrocarbon pipe work and fittings, utilities and any other significant fire hazards)
- Active/Passive Fire Protection Assessment (to assess for the adequacy of protection against escalation provided on vessels, pipe work, supports, and escape/evacuation routes, etc.)
- If applicable, Pipeline Risk Assessment (to ensure a systematic examination of the direct (internal and external influences) and escalated failure modes of pipelines in the immediate pipeline vicinity)
```

```text
## **3A-4.2.3.16.5 Flare Radiation Study**

CONTRACTOR shall conduct a Flare Radiation study to determine and assess heat fluxes and noise levels at manned areas on the PLANT. The scope should address all foreseeable continuous flaring modes (including COMMISSIONING modes), and maximum emergency flaring throughout.

CONTRACTOR shall conduct a Noise Verification study to check the noise emissions from the individual items of equipment against their noise specifications. The survey shall also evaluate whether areas should be classified as a Restricted Area where hearing protection must be worn or whether additional noise controls may be needed.
```

```text
## **3A-4.2.3.16.7 Human Factors Study**

CONTRACTOR shall conduct a Human Factors study to assess the interaction of personnel with the PLANT's SYSTEMS during normal operations and emergencies. The objective is to understand typical human responses to events and how they could affect levels of risks. CONTRACTOR shall utilize findings to influence aspects of the design and shall be used in the risk assessment. Ergonomic studies shall be carried out for Main Control Room.

Ergonomic design considerations and human factors shall be assessed to minimize the likelihood for human error for general control room operations, as well as emergency responses.

CONTRACTOR shall ensure that safe access is provided and arranged at appropriate height to facilitate production activities e.g. valve operation, pigging, routine maintenance and checks by Mechanical, Electrical and Control Engineering personnel. The design shall take into consideration the tasks to be performed.

All pressure, temperature and flow indicators shall be arranged so as to be clearly readable from permanent access decks/platforms.

Vessels or Tanks, where man access is allowed, shall have at least 2 manholes on each vessel of a minimum diameter of 24inch.
```

```text
## **3A-4.2.10 Faultless Right First Time Start-Up (FRFTSU)**

COMPANY emphasizes the importance of a faultless right first time start-up program for the PROJECT. CONTRACTOR shall plan and implement from the beginning of the EPC Phase the FRFTSU program for this PROJECT.

## **3A-4.2.10.1 Objective**

COMPANY and CONTRACTOR have the sole project goal of delivering the PLANT on time, without fault, and fully capable of efficient and safe first time right operational service. This encompasses a systematic approach to ensure a successful COMMISSIONING, start-up and first cycle operation of the facility. The philosophy goal is that the COMMISSIONING, start-up and first cycle operation is to be right the first time on schedule.

## **3A-4.2.10.2 Program Definition**

The formalized program to achieve the objective of world-class COMMISSIONING, start-up and operational performance for the total PROJECT, including first cycle operation.

The FRFTSU program will develop the process by which risk to this objective will be identified, assessed and addressed during the engineering, construction, MECHANICAL COMPLETION (including pre-Commissioning) and COMMISSIONING in a pro-active manner.

## **3A-4.2.10.3 Work Process**

The FRFTSU work process involves the sequence described below. CONTRACTOR's implementation plan and approach shall be based on a similar work process.

## **Management Team Orientation and Kick-Off**

- Identify and define Critical Success Factors (CSFs)
- Organize CSFs into discipline teams
- Establish risk likelihood and impact severity guidelines
```

```text
# **ATTACHMENT 3A-5.1.1 OPTIMIZATION AND BASIC STUDIES**

Annexure 3A-5 Rev. 0

Abu Dhabi Gas Liquefaction Company Ltd (ADNOC LNG)

#### **1.0 INTRODUCTION**

#### **1.1 Purpose**

This document provides a general specification for Optimization or Basic Studies to be used for COMPANY PROJECTS. It defines the minimum technical content, format for presentation and required actions by the CONTRACTOR as a result of the Study findings.

#### **1.2 Scope**

Optimization or Basic Studies are generally performed either at the feasibility stage or FEED stage of a PROJECT. However, this does not preclude the requirement for a Study in a later stage of the PROJECT cycle. This specification is applicable to all studies performed on behalf of COMPANY whether at the feasibility, FEED, EPC or other stages of a PROJECT.

This document defines the minimum requirements for Optimization and Basic Studies. As is often the case, any particular study may require more detailed analysis than is specified here. Compliance with these minimum specifications shall in no way relieve CONTRACTOR of his responsibility to provide an Optimization or Basic Study that is complete and of the highest Quality. CONTRACTOR shall use sound engineering judgment and shall conform to accepted industry practice in every aspect of his work.

All Optimization or Basic Studies shall be subject to COMPANY approval in terms of technical content, presentation and conclusions reached. The minimum requirements as stated in this specification shall not be relaxed unless a waiver is granted by COMPANY in writing.
```

```text
## **1.3 Document Organization**

This document is organized into four sections:

Section 1.0, this section, defines the purpose, scope and document organization of this document.

Section 2.0, General Requirements, defines the purpose of an Optimization or Basic Study and the minimum requirements for technical content.

Section 3.0, Presentation and Format, defines how the Optimization or Basic Study is to be formatted and presented to COMPANY.

Section 4.0, Document Submission Requirements defines the submission requirements for Optimization and Basic Studies.

### **2.0 GENERAL REQUIREMENTS**

## **2.1 Purpose of an Optimization or Basic Study**

The purpose of an Optimization or Basic Study is to evaluate multiple Options with regard to the implementation of a certain requirement, evaluate the most promising of these options in detail, and to reach a valid conclusion about how to best proceed with the implementation. The Optimization or Basic Study is intended to define the direction of all subsequent engineering development. It is also intended to provide an early check on scope and Quality so that COMPANY can ensure that all requirements are being met.

Typical examples of Optimization or Basic Studies include, but are not limited to:

- Process Equipment Selection Studies
- Process Flow Scheme Optimizations
- Control System Hierarchy Studies
- Advanced Process Control Strategies
- Process Unit Layout Optimizations
- Pipeline Corrosion Protection Studies
- Pipeline/Compressor Sizing and Optimization
- Process Simulation Studies
- Construction / Modularisation Studies
```

```text
## **3.0 PRESENTATION AND FORMAT**

#### **3.1 General**

This section defines the presentation and format requirements for Optimization and Basic studies. Included is a prototype table of contents, followed by a brief discussion of the layout and contents required for each section.

## **3.2 Document Format**

The Optimization or Basic Study shall be packaged in a stand-alone manner and shall generally be laid out as follows:

Cover Sheet (Title Page)

Table of Contents

Executive Summary

Introduction

Summary of Available Options

Analysis of Option 1

Analysis of Option 2

Analysis of Option N

Conclusions

Attachment 1

Attachment 2

Attachment N

#### **3.3 Proforma Table of Contents**

Section 3.2 on the previous page illustrates a pro-forma table of contents for an Optimization or Basic Study. The following paragraphs describe each of the sections in more detail.

## **3.3.1 Executive Summary**

This section shall be written as a 1 page abstract of the study intended for mid and upper level management that are not technical specialists. It shall provide a brief overview of the study and shall include all important recommendations and conclusions.

## **3.3.2 Introduction**

This section shall provide a complete introduction to the study as per the prototype table of contents. The purpose of this section is to tell the reader what the study is for, the limitations of the study, and how the study is organized.
```

```text
#### **1 GENERAL**

#### **1.1 INTRODUCTION**

ADNOC LNG (hereinafter called COMPANY) operates three (3) gas processing Trains in Das Island to produce LNG, LPG, Paraffinic Naphtha, and Sulphur. The Das Island facilities receive the feed gas from ADNOC OFFSHORE. Trains 1 & 2 were built in 1974-1976 with production capacity of 2.9 million tons/year of Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG). The 3rd LNG Train was built in 1991-1994 with an annual capacity of 3.2 million tons.

The Trains were commissioned in 1976. In year 2000, a study was undertaken (called Plant Integrity, Reliability and Recertification or PIRR) to extend the operational life of LNG Trains 1 and 2 to year 2019. Thereafter, the Operational life of Trains 1&2 was again extended to 2024 with required replacement / rejuvenation of the systems.

Majority of the process equipment, vessels and columns were replaced during the LNG Trains 1&2 Turnarounds which will have remnant life well beyond 2024.

As part of strategic requirement, ADNOC LNG launched in 2018 its Asset Longevity Program to extend the operation life of its three (3) LNG Trains year 2040. The Asset Longevity Program comprises of the following Work Streams:
```

```text
#### ❖ **Work Stream 2: (Trains 1& 2 Turnaround)** [By COMPANY]

o Including Fixed TA Scope + Variable Scope [R&Rs for Piping, Pressure Vessels, Boilers, MCHE, Machinery, etc.]

#### ❖ **Work Stream 3: (LNG Trains 1 & 2 Rejuvenation Works)** [**By Rejuvenation Project**]

o Trains 1&2 Utilities and Equipment Repairs that require common two train shutdown
```

```text
#### **1.2 PROJECT OBJECTIVE**

The objective of the Project is to Repair / Rejuvenate LNG Trains 1 & 2 identified equipment, and extend the operation life till year 2040. Also, the Project objective is to optimize the common shutdown related work duration in order to avoid consequent production losses to the COMPANY, while maintaining the Plant reliability and availability.
```

```text
#### **2.1.5 INSTRUMENTATION (WP7)**

Scope of Work for Instrumentation (work pack 7) package shall cover following:

- Replace existing CCC Compressor controllers (Series 3) with CCC prodigy rack & cardbased system
- Replace obsolete ESD valves (Total 62 Nos. 31 in each Train) along with its actuators and accessories, with new like-for-like ESD valves (with same face to face dimensions). The new ESD Valves shall have the same PFD (probability of failure on demand) values and Test interval also same as that of the existing Valves (Refer SIL Verification Report attached with Instrument Design Basis).
- Utility (Instrument Air) Tie-ins of replaced ESD valves
- Replace Plant-43 fire water pumps local control panels (2 Nos.)
- Replace MRB critical components (Relays, Diodes and Terminal Blocks) with new ones, in SS-T1/T2/U Marshalling Relay Boxes
- Replace CW pump hydraulic discharge valves including local control panels, associated tubing and branch cables (Note: During replacement of valves, alternate sea water supply to the hypochlorite plant is required. To facilitate the same, a cross-over line (8" NB, cement lined piping of approximate 10 m length), will be installed between 38-WC-0901-32" and 42-WC-0014-8")
- Replace obsolete Plant-42 band/bar screen control system with new system
- Replace control valve (CV) pneumatic positioners with smart positioners
- Utility (Instrument Air) Tie-ins of replaced CV Smart positioners
- UPS power sourcing for instrumentation at Outstations-3, 4, 5 & 7
```

```text
#### **2.7 OPTIONAL SCOPE**

#### **2.7.1 LEAK DETECTION SYSTEM**

COMPANY intends to install Leak Detection System (LDS) for online monitoring of trends towards leaks in the CW and FW network. Various leak detection technologies available in the industry were evaluated as part of FEED.

EPC scope includes verification and installation of Acoustic Based External Leak Detection System for the entire CW and FW piping network.

All factors like pipe network (not pipeline), ATEX certification, installation feasibility etc. shall be considered while designing leak detection system for CW and FW pipe network.

During EPC Stage, EPC CONTRACTOR shall:

- 1. Site survey existing cooling water and fire water network along with the leak detection system vendor
- 2. Prepare detailed Specification
- 3. Obtain and review Technical and Commercial proposals for the Acoustic Emission-based LDS
- 4. Prepare Technical and Commercial Bid Evaluation Reports
- 5. Detail engineer, Inspect and ship to site, new LDS
- 6. Install leak detection system on piping network and commission the system

For detailed requirements and scope, refer Scope of Work for Acoustic Emission Based Leak Detection System for Cooling Water and Firewater Piping (WP1), Doc. No.: RJ-100-A4J-0-00352- 0001.

## **2.7.2 ZONE-1 AND ZONE-2 CW/FW PIPING**

Referring to the scope of work addressed in UNDERGROUND CEMENT LINED PIPING (WP1), section 2.1.1, COMPANY intends to keep the zone-1 and zone-2 piping scope of work under optional lump sum, due to the Operational requirements.
```

```text
## **5.2 SITE SURVEY AND DATA VERIFICATION**

EPC CONTRACTOR shall mobilise an expert team including all Engineering and Project team members, to review and submit the requirements along with the checklist to COMPANY for the site survey and data verification. This review shall require EPC CONTRACTOR's personnel to perform a detailed visit to the site / worksite in order to collect all relevant data, Documents and drawings (whichever not available from COMPANY office) and physically check and become thoroughly familiar with the existing facilities. This shall include but not limited to:

- 1. Familiarize with the existing facilities, their operation, constraints and regulations.
- 2. EPC CONTRACTOR shall verify the existing as-built drawings. In case as-built drawings are not available or not matching with the existing arrangement, then CAD drawings shall be developed for the necessary EPC progress with no cost or schedule impact on this account.
- 3. Check and confirm the locations, sizes and extent of the existing facilities to be modified or removed as applicable in order to carry out the modifications and installation work for the new installations.
- 4. Check the location of equipment necessary to be removed/ relocated temporarily or permanently to carry out modification and installation work.
- 5. Check and confirm the feasibility of installation of all equipment, as well as mechanical handling of equipment and necessary access. Wherever feasibility cannot be established, EPC CONTRACTOR shall propose alternative solutions to be implemented at no extra cost.
```

```text
#### **5.6.4 PIPING STRESS ANALYSIS**

- All stress analysis reports from FEED stage shall be considered as preliminary and is provided to the EPC CONTRACTOR for "Information" only.
- EPC CONTRACTOR shall review and verify FEED stress analysis report provided by COMPANY. Verification and validation of stress analysis shall be done in early stage of EPC phase. COMPANY approval on stress analysis report shall be obtained prior to proceeding with issuing of final piping isometrics. Stress analysis shall be updated based on the final adopted routing.
- Pipe work shall be adequately designed to allow for thermal expansion, movements imparted from connected piping and loading during testing and normal operating. All the load cases associated shall be considered in the stress analysis.
- EPC CONTRACTOR shall carry out a comprehensive stress analysis of the piping system including full dynamic analysis as per the requirements of the COMPANY SPECIFICATION. An interim report containing all necessary information along with native CAESAR II files shall be submitted for COMPANY's review and comments before proceeding with the final report. CAESAR II native files shall also be submitted along with final report for COMPANY's final approval.
```

```text
- Tie-in locations identified on the drawings during FEED shall be further verified during detail engineering. EPC CONTRACTOR shall carry out SITE visits by their engineering and construction team and ensure all details (including isolation and shutdown requirements, hydro testing etc.) is feasible at the proposed locations. EPC CONTRACTOR shall fully design the tie-ins, including detail drawings, piping general arrangements and isometric drawings (construction and demolition for all sizes).
- EPC CONTRACTOR shall issue tie-in schedule and tie-in strategy documents showing details for each of the piping tie-ins with sketches both for construction and demolition. Final tie-in locations and details shall be agreed with COMPANY and approved prior to execution.
- Hot work shall be avoided (welded tie-in to be avoided) wherever practically possible and the use of prefabricated and tested flanged spools maximised. Tie-in drawings must show both new lines and existing line modifications required in order to complete the tie-in.
```

```text
## **8.3 SIMULTANEOUS OPERATIONS (SIMOPS)**

Simultaneous Operation (SIMOPS) will occur continuously with construction activities. SIMOPS Procedures will therefore be required to be followed for the safe integration of production activities with construction activities.

WORK activities must be carefully planned and executed such that one activity does not adversely affect another activity. If it is anticipated that activities being considered cannot satisfy this fundamental criterion, task rescheduling is the preferred course of action. Where tasks cannot be rescheduled and Simultaneous Operations (SIMOPS) are necessary, the potential increased risk of conducting work activities simultaneously and in close proximity must be understood and ultimately reduced to a level that is As Low as Reasonably Practicable (ALARP) as agreed by COMPANY designated SIMOPS authorities.

EPC CONTRACTOR shall note that SIMOPS was carried out during FEED and the same shall be reviewed and updated as required to capture detailed design development / construction activities.
```

```text
- e) Pre-Commissioning of electrical equipment shall as a minimum include the following:
  - No load run of motor for at least 4 hr and all related tests.
  - Energization of transformer without load & related tests.
  - Energization of isolation transformer & motor (decoupled) connected. Various speed ranges & no-load test shall be tested during this stage. The motor shall run for at least 4hr.
  - Energization of LV switchgears / DB's without load, feeder cable disconnected and with all outgoing feeder breakers/isolators open/isolated and padlocked.
  - All Site testing of LV & Control cables with both ends disconnected.
  - Complete testing (as per VENDOR recommendation) of UPS and batteries. This shall include discharge tests of batteries and final charging of batteries to its full capacity. All outgoing feeder cables shall be disconnected during above tests and outgoing feeder breakers kept open and padlocked.
  - Removal of cable & re-connecting from the equipment during pre-commissioning shall be in the scope of EPC CONTRACTOR.
  - Testing equipment shall be latest state of the art and cover associated testing parameter range for simulation of conditions occurring during normal and abnormal operation in the system.
  - All testing results shall be recorded as per COMPANY agreed format and counter signed by COMPANY representative.
  - All supporting test and pre-commissioning documentation such as records of tests, certificates, and calibration sheets shall be compiled in a documentation dossier.
```

```text
## **8.4.3 CIVIL / STRUCTURAL**

Construction scope of work for civil structural works consists of, but not limited to:

- 1. Earthwork in excavation for all types of soils and providing necessary shoring and strutting.
- 2. Back-filling at all depths with selected and approved earth available. Transportation and disposal of top unsuitable materials, breaking and removal of existing concrete elements, etc., shall be in accordance with COMPANY standards & procedures. The disposal shall be at the COMPANY approved designated locations. The excavated portion shall be properly levelled, filled with suitable materials and compacted to match with adjacent areas as per the project specifications.
- 3. PCC works included lean concrete at all depths below foundations of all types.
- 4. Reinforced concrete (RCC) works in sub-structure for foundations of all types, drains, trenches etc (as applicable). at all depths.
- 5. Centring and Shuttering in sub-structure at all depths and in super structure at all heights and elevations.
- 6. Dismantling/Demolishing of PCC/RCC, structural steel works for all depths and heights including disposal of unserviceable item at location as directed by COMPANY.
- 7. Structural steel including fabrication, erection and preparation of detailed fabrication drawings for all types of structures at all locations and heights in super structure.
- 8. Painting of Structural steel as per COMPANY Specifications.
- 9. Providing concrete protection below and above ground as per COMPANY specifications.
```

```text
#### **8.4.3.3 CONSTRUCTION SUPERVISION AND MANAGEMENT OF CIVIL AND STRUCTURAL WORKS**

The construction supervision and management of civil and structural works and other related services to be performed by the EPC CONTRACTOR for the new facilities shall include but not limited to the following:

- 1. Provide temporary facilities and safety arrangements required for the safe construction of the proposed utilities.
- 2. Where specifications or standards are not available, prepare PROJECT specific selfcontained and standalone specification or standards for COMPANY approval.
```

```text
#### **8.12.1 PRECAUTIONS AGAINST DAMAGE OR LOSS**

Load-out, including the packaging and protection of all items to be transported, shall be carried out in accordance with recognised good engineering practice. Proper protective materials, including timber, temporary framing and holding down wires shall be utilised to the satisfaction of the MWS. EPC CONTRACTOR shall pay particular attention to the correct positioning of items on board the transportation craft and to the sealing of all open ends of pipework, valves etc.

Great care shall be taken to avoid damage to protective coating during loading out and sea fastening. Pre-fabricated assemblies shall be secured on the cargo barge and loose items shall be placed on timber and secured. All items must be handled in a manner which is not detrimental to the protective coating, if any. If required, web slings shall be used otherwise lifting lugs shall be provided. Where it is necessary to use wrap around wire ropes for lifting, handling or securingproper use of padding and spreaders must be made to avoid damage to the coatings.

EPC CONTRACTOR shall further make sure at the load-out location that:

- 1. All materials and structures required for installation are included in the load-out, and
- 2. All structures, pipes, modules and other items are sea fastened in the manner indicated on the approved drawings, or as otherwise instructed by MWS.
```
